annotations.text:
Direction: regulated financial services.

Deep navy #12293D carries the chrome and every primary action; a single restrained gold #C9A227 marks the current place and the environment. Status colour is deep and desaturated — nothing shouts. Source Serif 4 for headings gives the documentary weight that category expects; Public Sans (drawn for government interfaces) does the UI; IBM Plex Mono carries locators and ids, which this product is full of.

Not Guardian's own palette, wordmark or brand assets — those are theirs.

Everything on these screens is your real content: the five use cases from your database, the actual locator syntax, the UUID dropdown values, the s7 failure and its page census.

Two things to decide:
• The product is still called "Browser Agent" in the chrome — the agent is gone, so that name may want revisiting.
• The environment chip (UAT) is new. It follows from the promotion work and I would argue it should be permanent — an operator should never be unsure which environment they are about to run a batch against.

Existing structure kept: same four sections, same top navigation. The change is the visual language, not the information architecture — so this reads as a restyle you can adopt incrementally rather than a rebuild.

The repair panel is drawn in its resolved state, showing the fix, the locator ladder change, and the line confirming it will be remembered — the piece that was missing until this week. The recorded locator is shown kept beneath the new one, because that is what actually happens.
